title: Strongyloidiasis (larvae in sputum, steroids, endemic origin): acquired by larval skin penetration
vignette: A 25-year-old woman comes to the office due to a week of cough and dyspnea. She also reports intermittent, crampy abdominal pain and diarrhea. The patient has no history of respiratory illness or other chronic medical conditions but was recently diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia that resolved with high-dose glucocorticoid therapy. She does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. She immigrated to the eastern United States from Myanmar 8 years ago, but has not travelled recently. Temperature is 37.2 C (99 F), blood pressure is 120/78 mm Hg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 18/min. Physical examination shows scattered wheezes and a nontender abdomen. Laboratory studies reveal eosinophilia, and sputum microscopy shows motile rhabditiform larvae. This patient most likely acquired the pathogen via which of the following modes of transmission?

clues.text: immune thrombocytopenia that resolved with high-dose glucocorticoid therapy
clues.note: Glucocorticoids suppress the immune control that normally keeps chronic Strongyloides in check, precipitating hyperinfection with pulmonary and GI symptoms.

clues.text: immigrated to the eastern United States from Myanmar 8 years ago
clues.note: Strongyloides is endemic in Southeast Asia; its autoinfection cycle can persist for DECADES, so infection acquired years earlier can flare with immunosuppression.
Peripheral eosinophilia points to a helminth (parasitic worm) infection.

clues.text: sputum microscopy shows motile rhabditiform larvae
clues.note: Finding LARVAE (not eggs) in sputum is characteristic of Strongyloides stercoralis, whose larvae migrate through the lungs.

whatMatters: Larvae in sputum + eosinophilia + steroid-precipitated pulmonary/GI symptoms + Southeast-Asian origin = STRONGYLOIDIASIS. Strongyloides stercoralis is acquired when soil-dwelling FILARIFORM LARVAE PENETRATE THE SKIN (walking barefoot on contaminated ground). Answer C.
strategy: Identify Strongyloides (larvae in stool/sputum, eosinophilia, autoinfection, hyperinfection with steroids) and recall its skin-penetration route (shared with hookworm). Reject vector routes: mosquito bite (malaria/arboviruses - blood parasites, not sputum larvae), tick bite (Lyme/Rickettsia), oocyst ingestion (protozoa like Giardia/Cryptosporidium - not multicellular worm larvae), and spore inhalation (fungi like Histoplasma - no helminth larvae in sputum).

eliminations.label: Mosquito bite - malaria/arboviruses
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: vector-borne transmission (e.g., malaria, dengue). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: these cause febrile blood-borne illness, not a helminth with larvae in the sputum and eosinophilia. ✅ Correct if: cyclic fevers with a blood smear parasite (malaria).

eliminations.label: Tick bite - Lyme/Rickettsia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: tick-borne transmission (Borrelia, Rickettsia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not produce nematode larvae in sputum; presentations are rash/systemic, not eosinophilic helminthiasis. ✅ Correct if: erythema migrans (Lyme) or spotted-fever rash.

eliminations.label: Oocyst ingestion - protozoa
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: fecal-oral ingestion of protozoan oocysts (Giardia, Cryptosporidium). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: protozoa are single-celled; sputum microscopy showing LARVAE indicates a multicellular helminth (Strongyloides), which enters via skin. ✅ Correct if: watery diarrhea with cysts/oocysts on stool O&P.

eliminations.label: Spore inhalation - fungi
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: inhaled fungal spores (Histoplasma, Aspergillus). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: fungi can cause eosinophilia and pulmonary symptoms but would not show helminth LARVAE in sputum. ✅ Correct if: pulmonary fungal infection with organisms/yeast, not worm larvae.

reasoning: Larvae (not eggs) in sputum + eosinophilia = Strongyloides stercoralis
Southeast-Asian origin (endemic) with autoinfection allows persistence for years
High-dose glucocorticoids precipitated hyperinfection (pulmonary + GI symptoms)
-> Strongyloides is acquired by filariform larvae penetrating the skin; answer C
mechanism: STRONGYLOIDES STERCORALIS is a soil-transmitted helminth endemic to Southeast Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, and the tropics. Infection occurs when FILARIFORM LARVAE in fecally contaminated soil PENETRATE THE SKIN (e.g., walking barefoot), enter the bloodstream/lymphatics, reach the alveoli, ascend the tracheobronchial tree, are swallowed, and mature into adult worms in the duodenum/jejunum. Unique among helminths, Strongyloides has an AUTOINFECTION cycle: some rhabditiform larvae mature into infective filariform larvae WITHIN the host and re-penetrate the intestinal mucosa or perianal skin, allowing the infection to persist for DECADES. Many hosts are asymptomatic, but IMMUNOSUPPRESSION - especially GLUCOCORTICOIDS - triggers HYPERINFECTION/dissemination with heavy larval migration causing cough, wheeze, dyspnea, crampy abdominal pain, diarrhea, and peripheral EOSINOPHILIA; larvae may be seen in stool or SPUTUM. The vector- and ingestion-based routes describe unrelated pathogens (malaria, Lyme, protozoa, fungi).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > Strongyloides stercoralis: filariform larvae penetrate skin; pulmonary migration; autoinfection (persists years); hyperinfection with steroids/immunosuppression; eosinophilia; treat ivermectin.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Larvae in sputum + eosinophilia + steroids + endemic origin = Strongyloides -> skin penetration.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Strongyloides, filariform vs rhabditiform larvae, autoinfection, hyperinfection, or eosinophilia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Mosquito/tick = vector-borne; oocyst ingestion = protozoa; spore inhalation = fungi - none give worm larvae in sputum.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Sputum microscopy (stem image): motile worm LARVAE (not eggs/protozoa) = Strongyloides migrating through the lungs -> skin-penetration route.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Strongyloides + steroids = hyperinfection; skin-penetrating filariform larvae; autoinfection persists for years.

keywords.back: Larvae = Strongyloides; eggs = most other helminths

firstAid.detail: Micro: skin-penetrating filariform larvae; pulmonary migration; autoinfection.
Micro > vector, ingestion, inhalation map to other pathogen classes.

memoryHook: Strongyloides walks in through the soles of bare feet, tours the lungs, and lurks for years - until steroids let it swarm (larvae in the sputum).
